title: Apple is testing daily usage limits for more complex Siri AI interactions
content:
Apple released betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3 today, and the company is using the update to test new per device daily usage limits for some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features, according to MacRumors.
Apple is testing daily usage limits for more complex Siri AI interactions
Frequent users of some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features will require an iCloud Plus subscription to avoid limits.
Basic Siri commands and requests will remain free and unlimited, but more advanced features that rely on cloud-based processing like generating, cleaning up, or extending images in Photos will be subjected to the daily limits. There are four categories of limited usage, MacRumors reports, including using Siri AI for “multi-step, personal context requests,” image generation and editing tools, automations in Shortcuts that “rely on Apple Foundation Cloud and Cloud Pro Models,” and third-party apps that use those same cloud models.
Apple hasn’t specified exactly how many times those features and tools can be used each day before limits are reached, but they’ll vary based on the task. The company reportedly plans to provide notifications when users are approaching their limit and have finally reached it.
Instead of having to wait until midnight each day for your usage to reset, most of Apple’s existing iCloud Plus plans (excluding the 50GB option) will include higher daily limits at their same price. The $2.99/month 200GB subscription includes 2x the usage, the $9.99/month 2TB plan includes 5x the usage, while the $29.99/month 6TB and $59.99 12TB/month options bump the usage limit to 10x and 20x, respectively. Family members sharing an iCloud Plus subscription will have a shared usage pool that’s used on a first come, first served basis.
Last week Apple updated Logic Pro with an option to “Buy More Usage” for that app’s intelligent assistant through $49.99 Intelligence Usage Packs that are expected to be added to other Apple Creator Studio apps this month, including Pixelmator Pro, Final Cut Pro, Motion, plus Pages, Keynote, and Numbers.

report.summary: Apple is testing daily caps on advanced Siri and Apple Intelligence cloud features, with higher limits tied to iCloud Plus subscriptions.
report.background: Apple has been rolling out Apple Intelligence across its devices, mixing on-device processing with cloud models for more demanding tasks. Cloud-based AI is expensive to run, and Apple is now experimenting with usage-based limits similar to how other AI providers meter heavy use. The move follows Apple's broader push to monetize AI features through subscriptions and add-on purchases rather than making all advanced capabilities free. By tying higher daily limits to iCloud Plus tiers, Apple can offset cloud compute costs while encouraging upgrades. The earlier Logic Pro 'Intelligence Usage Packs' suggest Apple is exploring multiple pricing models, from subscription multipliers to one-time usage top-ups, as it figures out sustainable economics for consumer AI.
key_points: Basic Siri commands and simple requests remain free and unlimited. The daily caps apply only to more advanced features that rely on cloud processing, such as generating, cleaning up, or extending images in Photos. Apple is drawing a line between lightweight on-device assistance and compute-heavy cloud AI.

MacRumors reports four limited categories: Siri AI multi-step personal-context requests, image generation and editing tools, Shortcuts automations using Apple Foundation Cloud and Cloud Pro models, and third-party apps that use those same cloud models. This means limits could affect both Apple's own features and external developers.

Apple has not specified exact daily quotas, saying they will vary by task. Users will reportedly get notifications as they approach and hit their limit. Instead of waiting for a midnight reset, iCloud Plus subscribers get higher limits: 2x on 200GB, 5x on 2TB, 10x on 6TB and 20x on 12TB. Family plans share a first-come, first-served pool.

Apple recently added a 'Buy More Usage' option to Logic Pro through $49.99 Intelligence Usage Packs, expected to expand to Pixelmator Pro, Final Cut Pro, Motion, Pages, Keynote and Numbers. This signals Apple is testing both subscription-based multipliers and one-time AI usage purchases across its software lineup.
report.impact: The test normalizes metered AI in consumer software. For the AI industry, it reinforces that cloud inference has real costs and that even Apple may not offer unlimited advanced AI for free. For developers, third-party apps relying on Apple's cloud models face uncertainty: heavy users could hit caps, so apps may need quota-aware design, clearer messaging, or fallback to on-device or third-party models. For regular users, casual Siri use stays free, but power users of image tools, complex Siri requests, and Shortcuts automations may need to pay more or manage usage. Shared family pools could create friction when one member consumes most of the allowance.
report.tools: Watch Apple's beta release notes and iCloud Plus plan details to see how quotas evolve. Test Shortcuts automations and Photos AI features to understand which tasks count. For cost control or offline alternatives, follow local AI tools such as Ollama, LM Studio, ComfyUI and Stable Diffusion, plus self-hosted chat interfaces like LibreChat. Apple Creator Studio apps including Logic Pro, Pixelmator Pro, Final Cut Pro, Motion, Pages, Keynote and Numbers are also worth monitoring for usage-pack pricing.
